themes.consensus_view: Banks agree central banks are raising interest rates to fight inflation caused by the Middle East energy shock, but they split on whether that shock lasts long enough to justify it, with Morgan Stanley and Academy seeing energy prices and rates staying higher while Allianz and JPMorgan expect the supply scare to fade as demand falls and stockpiles hold up.

facts_agreed.claim: Major central banks are tightening policy in response to energy-driven inflation, and desks expect the rate path to stay higher for now.
evidence_quotes: most major central banks – with the notable exception of the Bank of England – tightening policy.
there will be an attempt to run a restrictive monetary policy
For now, I think the path for energy prices (and stocks) and rates (globally) is higher.

facts_agreed.claim: Geopolitical supply disruption has distorted energy and shipping markets enough that desks are building a higher risk premium into their baselines.
evidence_quotes: shipping markets have been distorted by geopolitical disruptions.
incorporate features of a higher oil risk-premium into the baseline.

facts_agreed.claim: Desks across the corpus treat energy price shocks as the live transmission channel from the Middle East conflict into inflation and policy rates.
evidence_quotes: Energy price shocks and non-linear inflation impact
oil price shock transmission
Euro area energy price passthrough inflation
long-end yields sensitivity to energy prices
ECB monetary policy and gas price scenarios

facts_contested.claim: whether the energy shock is persistent or temporary
facts_contested.for_evidence: incorporate features of a higher oil risk-premium into the baseline.
facts_contested.against_evidence: we expect the shock to fade.

facts_contested.claim: whether the oil price premium is justified by actual physical tightness
facts_contested.for_evidence: incorporate features of a higher oil risk-premium into the baseline.
facts_contested.against_evidence: that $16 premium implies the market is pricing in the risk of an additional 4 mbd

themes.consensus_view: Banks across the corpus treat spending on AI computing hardware and data centers as the engine of megacap tech demand, but only Goldman stakes a direction, calling the largest tech stocks the most bought name on its book and its highest conviction trade.

facts_agreed.claim: Desks consistently tie megacap tech demand to the money being spent building AI computing capacity rather than to end-user product demand.
evidence_quotes: AI infrastructure investment
AI infrastructure capex commitments
AI-driven capital expenditure cycle
AI infrastructure buildout
Hyperscaler capital investment

facts_agreed.claim: Goldman reports the largest tech stocks were the most bought sector on its book and calls them the high conviction trade.
evidence_quotes: MegaCap Tech (GSTMTMEG) +168bps led the way and continues to be the high conviction trade.

facts_agreed.claim: Desks track the borrowing that funds the AI buildout as a separate strand of the same theme.
evidence_quotes: Hyperscaler AI infrastructure debt issuance
hyperscaler AI capex debt issuance
AI-related debt issuance
AI-related investment and issuance

themes.consensus_view: Almost every desk in this set says spending on AI data centers, chips and power is still growing and still earning back more than it costs to fund, with the only real pushback coming from a Bank of America survey where a record share of investors say companies are spending too fast.

facts_agreed.claim: AI infrastructure spending is the corpus's highest-conviction demand story, and the argument has moved from whether the demand is real to how big and how long it runs.
evidence_quotes: AI and digital infrastructure remain the firm's highest conviction investment themes.
discussions of this demand have moved beyond whether AI will create incremental demand
top performing themes of the year
Rising task volumes performed by agentic systems sustain demand for compute
The AI investment cycle remains well supported, with demand expanding beyond initial infrastructure build-out

facts_agreed.claim: Banks accept heavy near-term cash burn at the big cloud operators because the money being spent still earns more than it costs to borrow.
evidence_quotes: the return hurdle therefore remains wide enough to support continued investment.
negative free cash flow is perfectly fine provided that ROIC remains above the cost of capital.
We believe hyperscalers will prioritize capacity availability over near-term FCF optimization

facts_agreed.claim: Electricity supply, not chip supply, is treated as the binding constraint on how fast the build-out can proceed.
evidence_quotes: For the first time in three decades, global electricity demand is rising faster than economic output
discussions of this demand have moved beyond whether AI will create incremental demand

facts_agreed.claim: The spending is broadening out past graphics chips into processors, raw materials, data center landlords and the cost of running models rather than training them.
evidence_quotes: we continue to view agentic AI as a powerful demand accelerator that expands the CPU opportunity
AI is not just a semiconductor story, but increasingly a materials story
One call-out away from Semis / AI Infra has been the emergence of the “Inference Economy” theme
Demand fundamentals affecting listed operators such as DLR, EQIX, IRM, and NXT remain robust

facts_agreed.claim: AI capex is now large enough to move economy-wide numbers, from output growth to long-term interest rates.
evidence_quotes: Each year of expected capex through 2030 exceeds the whole dot-com telecoms boom
AI capex will continue to drive global GDP, supporting the equities of direct and indirect beneficiaries.
The structural factors pushing up r* are unlikely to subside.
AI is a bull market for duration in both scenarios

facts_contested.claim: whether companies are now spending too fast on the AI build-out
facts_contested.for_evidence: FMS investors say AI buildout “too fast” (record net 33% say companies overinvesting)
facts_contested.against_evidence: the return hurdle therefore remains wide enough to support continued investment.

facts_contested.claim: whether AI investment pushes long-term interest rates structurally higher or lower
facts_contested.for_evidence: The structural factors pushing up r* are unlikely to subside.
facts_contested.against_evidence: AI is a bull market for duration in both scenarios

facts_contested.claim: whether to add exposure to the AI build-out at current levels
facts_contested.for_evidence: AI and digital infrastructure remain the firm's highest conviction investment themes.
facts_contested.against_evidence: We remain cautious on adding meaningful exposure to the segment.

themes.consensus_view: The Bank of Japan has started lifting interest rates and the desks covering it read the central bank as intending to keep going, so the open question is how far and how fast, not whether more hikes come.

facts_agreed.claim: The Bank of Japan has shifted to raising rates with the stated aim of holding inflation down, and is expected to keep tightening.
evidence_quotes: the BOJ will continue to raise the policy interest rate and adjust the degree of monetary accommodation
Ueda explained a new focus on containing inflation rather than stimulating activity
